description: PathFinder routes many connectors together by *negotiated congestion*: connectors compete for channels (stretches of free space between obstacles) of limited capacity, and the ones with alternatives move away. Each iteration routes the connectors one by one with A*, and an edge costs more where its channel would be over capacity. After each iteration, the *history* cost of every overused channel grows and the *present* penalty doubles. Later iterations rip up and reroute only the connectors on an overused channel, until none is overused or an iteration limit is reached. It is a heuristic with no optimality guarantee; it reports the overuse that is left.

papers.title: PathFinder: A Negotiation-Based Performance-Driven Router for FPGAs
papers.venue: ACM Third International Symposium on Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA '95)
